subject: Operator guardrails and inter-zone failure model — QnA
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@sable.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sable Financial SecOps <sec-arch@sable.com>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operator guardrails & inter-zone failure model — security questionnaire

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Sable Security has a couple of targeted questions we need to close out for our board review next week. High level asks: a short network diagram showing control-plane vs data-plane demarcation for the Redwood inference runtime (including sidecars and KV cache paths), a concise summary of the isolation model between tenants, and a short threat-model that specifically addresses inter-zone failure modes that could cause fail-open egress.

Concretely, could you provide: 
- An annotated diagram (PDF) that labels CIDR/peering boundaries, bastion/egress relays, and where operator interaction is required.
- A one-page failure-mode summary that explains what happens when zone B loses access to the shared model cache (KV) and traffic shifts to other zones — including what operator actions are manual vs automated.
- Evidence of guardrails: operator runbooks, automated rollback thresholds, and any circuit-breaker telemetry we can use for audit.

We have a compliance cutoff for evidence on 2028-05-09. Is that achievable? If not, please propose an alternate timeline. Also please mark anything that is a design intent vs currently implemented.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Director, Security Engineering
Sable Financial

--
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@sable.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator guardrails & inter-zone failure model — security questionnaire

Alice — thanks and understood. High-level: we can deliver the annotated diagram and a targeted failure-mode summary by the 2028-05-09 cutoff. Below is a short preview of the requested items and a proposed delivery plan.

Summary preview (short):
- Control/Data-plane demarcation: control-plane (deployment orchestration, model rollouts, operator CLI) runs in a separate management VPC with strict egress rules; data-plane (inference runtime + KV cache) runs in segmented tenant subnets. Sidecars are deployed in the data-plane and terminate TLS to the model-serving process; operator access to sidecars is mediated through a bastionless jump-host with ephemeral certificates.
- Tenant isolation: network ACLs + per-tenant KV namespaces + runtime sandboxing. No cross-tenant KV access; shared model cache has per-tenant keys and rate-limits.
- Inter-zone fail-open scenario: if zone B loses KV access, requests are routed to zone A/C using a traffic-shifting policy with soft-fail thresholds. Automated throttling reduces burst fan-out; if traffic exceeds threshold, circuit-breakers return 429s to protect downstream storage. Operator runbooks define manual rollback to an older model snapshot or temporary capacity burn policy.

Proposed deliverables and timeline: 
- 2028-05-06: Annotated network diagram (PDF) + short threat-model summary (TXT).
- 2028-05-07: Egress/rollback playbook (MD) + operator runbook excerpt (TXT).
- 2028-05-09: Full evidence packet including telemetry examples (trace snippets) and a short recording of a runbook walkthrough (if required).

Open items for clarification: 
1) Do you prefer CIDR-level detail (we can provide a sanitized CIDR map) or conceptual boundaries only?
2) For audit telemetry, do you need raw traces or aggregated SLI/SLO-style graphs for submission?

I'll loop Vanessa and Ben on the artifacts delivery. If you want a 30-min walkthrough, we can schedule Monday.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

--
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@sable.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 May 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator guardrails & inter-zone failure model — security questionnaire

Karthik — thanks for the quick reply. A couple of clarifications: 
- Sanitized CIDR map is fine (labelled ranges is sufficient).
- For telemetry, aggregated SLI graphs plus a sample trace span is preferred. If you can include the query we used to derive the SLI, that helps.
- On the runbooks: can you explicitly call out the distinction between automated rollback vs operator-triggered rollback and whether rollback is model-version-based or deployment-configuration-based? That’s a key compliance ask.

If you can do the diagram + playbook by Monday 05/07 that would be ideal. I can make time for a 30-min call Monday afternoon.

Appreciate it,
Alice

--
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@sable.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 6 May 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Operator guardrails & inter-zone failure model — security questionnaire

Forwarding the package we discussed. Attached: annotated network diagram (sanitized), an egress/playbook that describes automated throttles and manual rollback procedures, and a 2-page threat-model summary that highlights mitigations for fail-open egress and supply-chain induced model drift.

Attachment stubs:
- network-annotated-diagram.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
- egress-playbook.md (Markdown, 6 pages)
- threat-model-summary.txt (Text, 2 pages)

Key implementation notes (excerpt):
- Automated rollback: triggered by anomaly detectors on token-failure rates and end-to-end latency. If anomaly thresholds are met for 2 consecutive 60s windows, an automated rollback to the last verified model snapshot is initiated (configurable; default is enabled for Dedicated and Private deployments).
- Operator-triggered rollback: available via the management plane CLI and documented in the operator runbook; this is model-version-based and requires a two-person approval for production rollbacks (or an elevated emergency override logged to audit).
- Circuit-breaker behavior: on cross-zone KV timeouts, we scale down cross-zone retries, enforce per-tenant rate ceilings, and return 429 until KV stabilization or operator intervention. This protects persistent storage and prevents cascade failures.

We also included the sanitized trace that shows a sample failover where traffic was shifted from zone B to zone A and the circuit-breaker prevented downstream overload (available in the Drive link).

Let us know if you want additional SLI graphs or raw trace spans. If all good, Karthik can book the Monday walkthrough with your team.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

--

[This message includes attached evidence files. If you need the original source diagram with CIDR detail for an auditor under NDA, we can coordinate an encrypted transfer.]
